section_map.title: Purpose
section_map.body:
This document defines the canonical vocabulary used by the **Document Identity** component.

Its purpose is to establish a common and unambiguous terminology for every architectural concept related to document identity within the Documentation Framework.

The definitions contained herein are normative for the Document Identity component and complement the framework-wide terminology defined in **DF-ARC-006 – Terminology**.

---

section_map.title: Introduction
section_map.body:
A shared architectural vocabulary is essential for ensuring consistency across specifications, implementations, integrations, and future framework evolution.

The terms defined in this document shall be interpreted exactly as described whenever they appear within the Document Identity component.

If a term is defined both in this document and in **DF-ARC-006**, the framework terminology remains authoritative. This document refines those definitions only within the scope of Document Identity.

---

section_map.title: Assignment
section_map.body:
**Definition**

The architectural act of associating a permanent Document Identity with a document.

**Notes**

- Occurs exactly once.
- Creates the canonical identity.
- Does not imply document approval or publication.

---

section_map.body:
**Definition**

The official identifier representing a Document Identity within the Documentation Framework.

**Notes**

- Unique.
- Permanent.
- Immutable.
- Referenceable.

section_map.body:

**Notes**

The architectural verification that a Document Identity satisfies every mandatory rule defined by the Documentation Framework.

section_map.title: Synonyms
section_map.body:
The following terms are considered equivalent within the scope of the Document Identity component.

| Preferred Term | Equivalent Expressions |
|----------------|------------------------|
| Document Identity | Canonical Identity |
| Identifier | Canonical Identifier |
| Identity Assignment | Identity Creation |
| Identity Retirement | Identity Decommissioning |
| Identity Reference | Document Reference |

The preferred terms shall be used throughout the Documentation Framework.

---

section_map.title: Prohibited Terminology
section_map.body:
The following expressions should be avoided because they may introduce architectural ambiguity.

| Avoid | Use Instead |
|--------|-------------|
| Document ID | Document Identity or Identifier (depending on context) |
| Internal ID | Identifier |
| Repository ID | Repository Identifier |
| File Identifier | Identifier |
| Database ID | Implementation Identifier |
| Temporary Identifier | Temporary Reference |

---

section_map.title: Naming Guidelines
section_map.body:
The following naming recommendations apply to all Document Identity specifications.

- Use **Document Identity** when referring to the architectural concept.
- Use **Identifier** when referring to its canonical value.
- Use **Identity Domain** when referring to the uniqueness scope.
- Use **Reference** when referring to architectural links between documents.
- Use **Assignment** only for the initial creation of an identity.
- Use **Retirement** only for the permanent end of an identity lifecycle.

---

section_map.body:

Framework terminology remains authoritative.

This document introduces only component-specific vocabulary required by the Document Identity component.

section_map.body:
The Document Identity Dictionary establishes the canonical vocabulary for the Document Identity component.

It provides precise architectural definitions for the concepts, properties, lifecycle states, validation terms, governance concepts, and identity-related terminology used throughout the component.

By maintaining a consistent vocabulary, this dictionary supports interoperability, architectural consistency, unambiguous communication, and long-term maintainability across the entire Documentation Framework.

literal_comparison_clauses.text:
# 1. Introduction

This glossary provides the common consultation and convergence vocabulary for the Documentation Framework. Entries identify subjects, contexts, controlled aliases and responsible source meanings; they do not transfer every domain’s semantic authority to Terminology.

Architectural sources use applicable canonical meanings and identify qualified contexts or deviations. Existing conflicts and incomplete owner contracts remain recorded for reconciliation. Consistent communication is an assessed objective, not a guarantee established by a glossary’s presence.

---

# 2. Purpose

The primary responsibility is terminology consultation: identify meanings and distinctions, reference responsible contracts, and support traceable architectural usage and evolution. Therefore Type is Reference; Family Architecture denotes the common documentary area, not an invented component or special Type.

The glossary preserves its original 39 term anchors, provides missing owner-linked model distinctions and separates normative authority, classification, operational implementation and evidence. It owns its common vocabulary organization/usage within the declared scope, without replacing detailed domain definitions or declaring all consuming sources consistent.

---

# 3. Scope

Applicable vocabulary concerns Foundation, Architecture, component specifications, Governance, reference material, roadmaps and Templates. Terms identify their subjects/contexts; domain-specific interpretation follows responsible owners and the adopted working rules. Detailed component and external DMS/CMS specifications are not supplied by this reference.

Every README.md, CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md at every location is a non-normalized functional file. Such names require no normalized Document ID, Family, Type, Component, Version, Revision, Status or Baseline by normalization. Their content, structure, references, inventory and hash evidence remain reviewable; the exclusion creates no exceptions to the four Types for normalized documents.

DF defines documentary contracts; DMS, tools or applicable manual processes execute management/checking operations. CMS governs changes in its own scope. A definition, normative statement, Type Reference or resolving reference proves neither approval, publication, snapshot inclusion nor implemented conformance.

---

# 4. Terminology Principles

Common terms preserve responsible owner meanings in a declared scope. Summaries and qualified usage do not become competing semantic authorities; unresolved conflicts remain explicit.

## 4.1. Canonical

Each concept/record has an identified responsible owner and authoritative contract within its semantic domain/scope. The glossary references those meanings; it does not make every copied definition canonical merely by restating it. Derived representations retain source/edition provenance.

---

## 4.2. Unambiguous

State the subject, domain and qualified context of a term. Formal contextual aliases map to one meaning; shared words across domains require qualification. Ambiguity and competing definitions are assessed from actual usage rather than prohibited by an unqualified one-word/one-concept claim.

---

## 4.3. Consistent

Preserve applicable meaning across consuming sources and traceable projections. Record owner conflicts, stale usage and incomplete propagation. An edited glossary alone proves neither integrated consistency nor conformity of unseen sources.

---

## 4.4. Stable

Definitions evolve through controlled, justified owner/consumer changes. Preserve compatible meaning where feasible; necessary incompatibility requires explicit impact, edition transition and verification. Stability does not forbid every justified revision or guarantee harmless extension.

---

## 4.5. Technology Independent

Architectural definitions avoid prescribing technology unless an integration constraint explicitly requires it. Actual representations, formats, storage adapters and executors still need applicable contracts and evidence; conceptual independence does not prove universal interoperability.

---

## 5.11. Document

A logical documentary entity with a purpose and a coherent unit of represented knowledge. File and physical location are representations, not its logical key. Applicable normalized identity, Metadata, classification and edition-governance contracts apply only within normalization scope (§§3/5.56/5.57). An exact edition (§5.40) differs from the enduring logical document.

**Responsible role/source:** Document Identity for logical identity; Metadata/Classification/Governance for their respective meanings, as summarized by Concepts §5.3 (§9).

---

## 5.12. Document Identity

Permanent logical identity under the applicable Domain+Identifier allocation/preservation contract. Its identifier representation (§5.52) is not the entity itself. Filename, repository, title, classification, Version/Revision and Status do not automatically recalculate a valid identity. The adopted corpus representation DF-SSS-NNN uses a stable allocation series independent of current Family/Type; full DID source integration remains pending.

**Responsible role/source:** Document Identity; Document Identity Concepts, with working corpus syntax in Review Policy §4 (§9). No new allocation or migration is performed here.

---

## 5.16. Governance

Applicable contracts for responsibilities, controlled evolution, decisions and required evidence. Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines define distinct capability roles; an applicable DMS/tool/manual process executes operations, and CMS supplies change evidence within its own scope. Domain governance, document-edition Status, validation, approval, publication and Baseline membership remain separate.

**Responsible role/source:** Responsible domain Governance contracts and common Architecture summaries in Components §6 (§9).

---

## 5.17. Identity

The persistent characteristic/key by which an entity is recognized within its declared identity domain, independent of mutable properties. Identity is represented through an identifier but is not synonymous with the string representation. Document Identity (§5.12) is a qualified identity domain role; other endpoints use their own appropriate contracts and do not automatically receive normalized document IDs.

**Responsible role/source:** Relevant entity-domain owner; Document Identity Concepts §§3.3–3.5 for documentary identity (§9).

---

## 5.22. Lifecycle

The subject-specific states, transitions and evolution contracts of an identified entity or definition. Document editions, Metadata Elements, Classification definitions and Template entities can have distinct lifecycles with their own owners. A state list does not establish a universal Workflow graph, operational permission model or implementation maturity.

**Responsible role/source:** Relevant entity/domain lifecycle owner; Classification Lifecycle and common Workflow summaries provide explicit distinctions (§9).

---

## 5.40. Document Edition

An exact recorded state of a logical document, including represented content/descriptors and relevant context. Logical identity persists across editions; coordinates, Status and actual snapshot membership remain separate facts.

**Responsible role/source:** Document Identity for logical entity; documentary governance/Metadata for edition facts; Concepts §5.3 and Review Policy §5 (§9).

---

## 5.52. Identifier

Canonical representation used to reference an identity within its declared domain. A document’s DF-SSS-NNN representation uses stable allocation namespaces and a positive allocated number; its string is not the logical entity or current classification. Detailed syntax/allocation remains with the qualified identity contract.

**Responsible role/source:** Relevant identity-domain owner; Document Identity Concepts §3.4 and working Review Policy §4 (§9).

---

## 5.53. Identity Domain

Scope in which the applicable identity contract establishes uniqueness and allocation/preservation rules. Documentation Framework is the adopted documentary domain; other architectural entity kinds can use different qualified domain contracts. Domain+Identifier and exact-edition references are distinct.

**Responsible role/source:** Relevant entity-domain owner; Document Identity Concepts §3.5 and Review Policy §4 (§9).

---

## 5.56. Functional File

Within this corpus, every README.md, CHANGELOG.md or ArchitecturalMilestones.md at any location. Such files are not normalized and require no normalized identity/header/classification by that exclusion; legitimate existing information is not automatically deleted. Content, organization, references, inventory and hashes remain reviewable.

**Responsible role/source:** User-adopted scope and Review Policy §2 (§9); central logs retain their own record conventions.

---

## 5.57. Normalized Document

A documentary source within the applicable normalization scope, with the adopted identity, classification and edition/Metadata contracts. Functional names in §5.56 are excluded before applying those obligations; missing canonical Element/Profile records are not manufactured by declaring a source normalized.

**Responsible role/source:** Applicable document/Metadata/Identity/Classification contracts and Review Policy §§2–5 (§9).

---

# 6. Naming Conventions

Use canonical natural-language component names in prose, including their spaces and spelling (Document Identity, Knowledge Graph, Metadata Generator). Directory aliases, identifier syntax and programming PascalCase are separate representation conventions; this glossary mandates no concatenated prose names or filename/ID migration.

Use singular entity terms where appropriate without renaming plural capability owners: Baseline is an entity term, Baselines is the registered capability name. Define abbreviations before use. Preserve context-qualified terms, documented controlled alias mappings and legitimate historical vocabulary rather than rewriting past meaning.

| Contextual expression | Canonical target/meaning | Scope/limit |
|---|---|---|
| Architectural Component | Component (§5.7) | Same capability concept in common DF Architecture; original §5.2 anchor retained |
| Architectural Layer | Structural Layer (§5.21) | Same structural grouping; conceptual concerns remain a distinct view; original §5.3 retained |
| Framework | Documentation Framework (§5.14) | Short form only in declared DF context; original §5.15 retained |
| DocumentIdentity | Document Identity | Received directory alias, not a competing component name or recalculated ID |
| DMS / CMS | Qualified system-role terms in §§5.58/5.59 | External/contextual roles, not new registered DF components or complete specifications |

Aliases have explicit targets and contexts; historic or external spelling requires a map/qualification when relevant. New terms and changed meanings follow §§8/10 and their domain owners. No taxonomy, catalog record or identity allocation is performed by naming a term.

---

# 7. Forbidden Terminology

Avoid undefined abbreviations, unqualified domain overloads, competing definitions, unsupported semantic authority and technology-specific implementation labels presented as universal architectural concepts. Do not use a directory, classification label, projection or terminology entry to conceal actual required dependencies or an unresolved owner conflict.

Controlled aliases, canonical plural component names, qualified contexts and documented historical vocabulary are permitted under §6; they do not license arbitrary interchangeable meanings. Distinguish Template Type, Metadata value type and document Type explicitly. A semantic owner cannot be reassigned merely to make a dependency graph look acyclic.

---

# 8. Terminology Governance

New or changed terms identify the responsible domain/source, subject/context, previous/new meaning, rationale, affected consuming editions and applicable evidence. Working review rules derive from the user-adopted policy; received incompatible wording remains preserved as input/history rather than a second governing rule for the same operation.

Assess actual consumer propagation, compatibility and required contracts. Deprecated/historical meanings retain their mappings and source editions; formal removal or replacement does not erase prior records. Canonical authority follows responsible applicable contracts, not an informal glossary claim or approval inferred from Type Reference.

Actual contribution, user authorization, review, validation, ownership and approval are separate facts. Later human/tool edits require resulting-edition/byte assessment; a previous local PASS does not transfer automatically or assign responsibility for consequences of a changed final product.

---

# 10. Evolution Guidelines

Introduce a term only for a justified distinction not adequately represented by an existing qualified term or controlled alias. Record owner/subject/context, previous/new meaning, affected source editions, references and transition evidence before propagation. Avoid duplicate semantic authorities and title-derived classification.

Preserve compatible meaning where feasible. Necessary incompatible changes require explicit justification, consumer compatibility/required-contract assessment, versioned transition and verification. A new term or supplemental definition is not presumed harmless to every consumer.

For document editions in this working review, compatible correction retains Version, compatible additive capability increments minor, and incompatible contract change increments major/reset minor 0. Each changed persisted edition increments Revision monotonically across Version changes; unchanged-source validation increments neither coordinate and is tracked centrally. Domain-specific entity lifecycle/version rules remain separately qualified.

Local glossary correction does not certify complete terminology rollout, global acyclicity, owner catalog completeness or operational outcomes. Actual integrated checks remain separate work.

# 4. Scope

The component's scope includes identity concepts, models, elements/schema, constraints, identity lifecycle, validation, governance, typed relationships, assessed extensibility, specifications and examples. Detailed sources retain their responsibilities; this architecture does not invent a canonical merged field catalog or certify all peer requirements.

For applicable normalized documents, logical identity remains associated with the same document across ordinary content/descriptor, classification, representation, repository and document-edition changes. Exact edition coordinates, document Status, identity-record assignment/preservation/retirement evidence, maturity and Baseline membership are separate facts. A mutable state record is not a replacement for the stable identity key.

Unassigned concerns a pre-allocation subject, not an already assigned Domain+Identifier key. Retirement preserves allocated-number reservation, document association/history and reference interpretation; it does not guarantee a running resolver or retrievable content. Document lifecycle and identity-record lifecycle can have distinct subjects/contracts. The source does not prescribe a universal transition or permission graph.

DID-003/004/005/006/010/014 currently disagree on reference cardinality, mandatory State/Canonical Reference fields and identity state terminology. Those actual claims are preserved in §12.3 for full owner cycles. The architectural distinctions here neither merge incompatible schemas nor silently remove/add their mandatory fields. No Metadata Dictionary Element, Profile or canonical state record is fabricated.

---

# 5. Out of Scope

The following roles are separate from document identity semantic ownership. Area labels, registered capability contracts and operational executors are identified separately; naming an owner proves no implemented service.

| Received responsibility | Responsible contract/role | Operational or semantic boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Document metadata | Metadata plus applicable semantic domain owners | Dictionary defines, Schema organizes, Profile constrains and Instance supplies values under one effective Profile; descriptive representation does not replace identity |
| Document classification | Classification | Family/Type and other category meanings remain mutable and separately owned |
| Registry management | Registry | Catalog/lookup contracts and provenance; actual registration/lookup executed by an applicable system/process |
| Discovery services | Discovery area: Registry, Relationships, Knowledge Graph, Navigation, Search | Area groups capabilities; it is not another component or mandatory routing intermediary |
| Workflow management | Workflow and applicable Policies | Subject-specific transitions/rules; DMS/tool/manual operation, not an implemented DF workflow engine |
| Version control | Documentary edition contracts versus source-control systems/adapters | Version/Revision/Status semantics follow applicable governance/edition contracts; repository commits and Source Control Integration adapters do not define them |
| Repository management | DMS or other applicable external system | Organization, storage, permissions and physical-location execution |
| Storage technologies | Applicable implementations/external systems | Persistence mechanisms preserve applicable representation/provenance requirements |
| Identifier generation algorithms | Applicable allocation executor | Generate/allocate under identity-domain rules and collision/reservation evidence; no algorithm supplied here |
| Persistence mechanisms | Applicable implementation/external system | Store identity/edition/context records without acquiring identity semantics |

Governance is an area grouping Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines; it is not a single invented component owning all operational management. Reviews records examined scope/results; Baselines defines immutable selected exact approved editions and context. CMS change evidence does not substitute for documentary approval or snapshot inclusion.

---

# 7. Core Architectural Characteristics

Within its declared allocation/preservation contract, an assigned logical identity shall be unique for the document in its domain, stable through normal evolution, and never reassigned to a different document. Domain qualification is required to interpret uniqueness; an identifier string alone is not universally unique across unregistered domains.

Immutability concerns the assigned Domain+Identifier key under its applicable contract, not every mutable record about that identity. Identity-state evidence, references, location, descriptors and exact-edition coordinates can evolve under their own owner rules without automatically replacing the key. References and aliases interpret an existing logical document; they do not license another document to reuse its identity. Allocated and retired identities remain reserved.

Preserve valid assigned identity during ordinary classification, repository, format, lifecycle and edition changes. If a necessary authorized schema/ID migration would change an otherwise immutable representation/allocation contract, first assess and explicitly reconcile the governing previous/new rules with responsible identity/domain sources. Record old→new mappings, same-document continuity, aliases/reservations, collisions, historical/reference/context effects, exact source editions, affected consumers and transition verification before coordinated application. Preserve original representations and historical immutable snapshot selections; never retarget old members or reassign retired allocations to another document. No blanket permission for arbitrary identity changes or two contradictory governing rules for one operation is introduced. This localized UPDATE performs no migration.

Long-term understandable/referenceable identity is a requirement and design objective supported by qualified domain/canonicalization and actual preservation/resolution evidence. It guarantees neither universally understood bare strings nor future content availability. Exact-edition references additionally identify the intended Version/Revision and relevant bytes/context; logical identity alone selects neither an exact edition nor Baseline membership.

---

# 9. Component Relationships

The following are scoped architectural contract declarations for documentary uses. They do not establish an operational service call, every-component routing requirement or complete dependency graph.

| Consumer | Provider | Required contract/use | Source/scope boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metadata | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document described | DID-009 §5.1 declaration; descriptive values retain their own semantic owners |
| Classification | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document being classified | DID-009 §5.2; category/definition entity identity is a separate qualified contract |
| Templates | Document Identity | Identity of normalized Template documentation/document instances | DID-009 §5.3; Template definition/instance keys are not automatically DF document IDs |
| Registry | Document Identity | Logical document identity for a document catalog entry | DID-001 §9.4; source-edition provenance and exact lookup context required |
| Relationships | Document Identity | Identity of document endpoints | DID-001 §9.5; other endpoint kinds use their own domain contracts |
| Knowledge Graph | Document Identity | Logical document node identity | ARC-005 §12; typed edges remain Relationships records, not document identities |
| Baselines | Document Identity | Logical member identity | ARC-005 §12; exact edition/descriptive/context evidence additionally required |
| Workflow | Document Identity | Identified normalized document subject | DID-009 §6.1; applicable transition execution remains with the actual process |

## 9.1. Metadata

Identity identifies the logical document; Metadata defines/represents descriptors and owner meanings. Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance roles remain separate under one effective Profile. Identity data can be represented descriptively without transferring identity semantics or creating missing Metadata Element/catalog records.

**Unresolved reciprocal declarations:** supplied README states Document Identity→Metadata for descriptive concepts, while DID-009 §§5/10 states Metadata→Document Identity and no dependency on consuming components. Both source claims remain visible as required-dependency evidence pending owner/context/interface reconciliation. Distinguish core identity meaning from identity-record descriptor use, but do not silently downgrade a genuinely required contract into navigation or declare the apparent cycle resolved. Different stated uses alone do not prove operational independence or global acyclicity. Full Metadata/DID source cycles must establish the actual required scopes and cycle treatment under ARC-004.

## 9.2. Classification

Classification owns category meanings and uses identity when categorizing a normalized document. Current Family/Type/Component labels are independent from stable allocation series and do not automatically reconstruct an assigned valid ID. Classification definitions and their own lifecycle/keys are different subjects from document editions; their actual identity contracts need qualification. Nominal CLS-003/CLS-001 collision reconciliation remains scheduled, not corrected by this source.

## 9.3. Templates

Templates owns reusable documentary structures and definition/instance contracts. A normalized document describing or applying a Template can require document identity; Template entities and graph/relationship identifiers are not thereby allocated normalized document IDs. Templates consumes appropriate owner meanings without redefining document identity, Metadata or Classification. Source presence and using a Template prove neither consistency nor approved publication.

## 9.4. Registry

Registry catalogs/looks up identified documentary entities or editions under declared provenance and freshness/current-historical-snapshot context. It does not redefine identity. A document lookup needs its domain/canonical key; an exact-edition lookup additionally needs edition/context evidence. No universal Registry intermediary, implemented resolver or persistent content availability is implied.

## 9.5. Relationships

Relationships owns typed connection records and provenance; Document Identity owns the contract for document endpoints. Other endpoint kinds use their own qualified identity domains. Canonical document reference validity requires the intended document/edition context and actual evidence; logical reference preservation does not imply live-content retrieval. Required edges remain required even when their data comes through a projection; a reference label cannot conceal a genuine cycle.

## 9.6. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph projects identified entities and Relationships records with source/edition provenance and refresh limits. Document nodes use document identity; graph edges or non-document entities need appropriate other contracts. Projections do not create competing identity/relationship authority or certify complete network correctness. No Registry→Graph→Baseline execution chain is prescribed.

## 9.7. Governance

Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines define documentary transition, decision, review and snapshot requirements; actual operation remains with DMS/tool/manual processes and CMS change scope. Identity-record lifecycle, document Status/Version/Revision, maturity, review, validation, approval, publication and membership are distinct. A state list alone is neither a universal permission graph nor an implemented workflow.

Baselines selects an explicitly identified immutable set of exact approved document editions with relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Identity alone cannot select an exact member; eligibility, consistency and actual inclusion remain separate checks. Draft successors neither inherit membership nor retarget older snapshots. Retired identities preserve reservations/history without implying current document publication or resolver availability.

# 3. Core Concepts

The eleven received concept titles and numbered anchors are retained. Each definition identifies its subject/contract and an evidence boundary; these are conceptual distinctions rather than a populated element catalog, universal implementation guarantee or competing owner schema.

## 3.1 Document

A **Document** is a logical documentary knowledge entity under an applicable recognition and normalization scope. An exact document edition records particular content/descriptors and context; a file or representation is not the logical entity itself.

Normalized identity obligations apply after the functional-file exclusion in §2. Template definitions/instances, Metadata Elements and graph/relationship records can have other qualified entity contracts; not every knowledge asset or endpoint receives a DF document ID.

**Evidence boundary:** Identify the actual subject, scope and exact edition/representation examined. Distinguish valid logical identity from coordinates, Status, maturity and membership; registration or recognition alone proves neither approval nor complete conformance.

---

## 3.2 Document Identity

A **Document Identity** identifies the same logical document under a declared **Domain+Identifier** allocation/preservation contract. Uniqueness applies within that domain, not to every bare string in every external system. Identity remains associated with the document through ordinary changes and is not reconstructed from current classification, path or edition.

The assigned key, canonical identifier representation, mutable identity-record state and exact edition are separate. DID-001 establishes the applicable architecture; full peer schema integration remains pending.

**Evidence boundary:** Check domain qualification, actual allocation/reservation records, intended document continuity and examined source editions. No successful allocation, universal resolver or arbitrary key change is implied by the definition.

---

## 3.3 Identity

An **Identity** is the persistent characteristic/key by which an entity is recognized within its declared domain, independently of mutable properties under that contract. **Document Identity** is the qualified documentary application in this component; other entity kinds retain their own appropriate identity contracts.

Metadata can represent identity values while their semantic meaning remains owned by the identity domain. A descriptor, graph edge or Template entity is not automatically a normalized document.

**Evidence boundary:** Record the endpoint/entity kind and domain owner. Representation, source presence or repeated descriptive values do not create another identity, transfer semantic authority or allocate a new entity identifier.

---

## 3.4 Identifier

An **Identifier** is the canonical representation used to reference identity within its declared domain. The representation is not the logical document itself. Human/machine interpretation follows applicable domain, syntax, canonicalization and adapter requirements rather than universally understandable bare strings.

For this DF corpus, DF-SSS-NNN uses stable registered three-letter allocation series and a positive allocated number under DID-001/Review Policy. The series is independent of current Family/Type/path/Version/Revision. Detailed logical schema/constraint/specification owners supply actual representation contracts; this concept supplies no physical format or generation algorithm.

**Evidence boundary:** Check actual domain/representation rules and intended reference target. Preserve current owner discrepancies; do not infer arbitrary domain creation, a merged mandatory field schema or completed corpus migration from this synopsis.

---

## 3.5 Identity Domain

An **Identity Domain** is the declared scope in which the responsible contract establishes uniqueness, allocation and preservation rules. Documentation Framework is the adopted documentary domain, represented by DF. Equal numeric suffixes in different registered allocation series are not collisions when the qualified full identifiers differ.

Other-domain use needs explicit qualified owner rules and relevant registration/resolution/context evidence. An implementation does not silently create or redefine a DF-recognized domain merely by asserting uniqueness. DF syntax is not imposed on every external domain.

**Evidence boundary:** Identify actual domain owner, namespace/allocation evidence and collision scope. Gaps do not prove availability; allocated/retired numbers are not reused. This UPDATE performs no allocation, series registration, ID/path or domain migration.

---

## 3.6 Identity Lifetime

The **Identity Lifetime** concerns assignment, active use and preserved historical identity association under the applicable contract. Ending active document use or retiring/deleting an operational representation does not by itself erase retained identity history/reservations or permit reassignment to another document.

Identity-record lifecycle and document-edition lifecycle have different subjects. Unassigned describes a pre-allocation subject; retirement preserves reservation/history and reference interpretation, not evidence of current publication or live content retrieval. DID-004/006/014 state disagreements remain owner work.

**Evidence boundary:** Identify the actual active/historical/retired subject and preservation evidence. The concept does not prescribe an immortal storage implementation or guarantee future resolution/content availability; it preserves non-reuse and traceable historical association obligations.

---

## 3.7 Identity Stability

**Identity Stability** requires valid assigned identity to remain associated with the same document through ordinary content/descriptor, classification, repository, format, lifecycle and edition evolution. The key is stable under its governing allocation contract; mutable state/location/reference records do not automatically replace it.

Necessary authorized schema/ID migration that changes an otherwise immutable representation/allocation rule first explicitly reconciles governing previous/new contracts with responsible identity/domain owners. Record old→new mapping, same-document continuity, aliases/reservations, collisions, history/reference/context, exact editions, affected consumers and transition checks before coordinated application. Preserve historical immutable snapshot selections; no arbitrary reassignment or simultaneous contradictory governing rules is introduced.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess actual target continuity, representations and owner/consumer evidence. Stability supports preserved reference interpretation but does not ensure a running resolver or retrieved content. This localized UPDATE performs no migration.

---

## 3.8 Identity Uniqueness

**Identity Uniqueness** requires no two distinct logical documents to share the same assigned identity within the same declared domain. It is a qualified architectural obligation, not an outcome guaranteed by the concept definition or a Version label.

Canonical alias/reference representations resolve the intended existing logical identity under explicit rules; they do not license another document to reuse its allocation. Actual allocation/reservation and collision checks must examine current and historical records within their declared scope.

**Evidence boundary:** Identify domain, exact examined records and coverage, including aliases/reservations and unresolved collisions. A missing external history or partial scan does not prove global uniqueness or complete registry correctness.

---

## 3.9 Identity Permanence

**Identity Permanence** preserves assigned identity association with the same logical document across normal evolution and its applicable historical context. Allocated and retired identities shall not be reassigned to another document. Retirement or an unavailable file does not make the old allocation free.

Necessary controlled representation/allocation migration follows §3.7 without retargeting historical snapshot members, erasing original mappings or permitting retired-ID reuse. Logical identity and exact approved-edition selection remain distinct.

**Evidence boundary:** Check actual association, non-reuse/reservation history and relevant reference/edition context. Preservation is an obligation requiring evidence, not a guarantee that every historical document remains actively published or retrievable.

---

## 3.10 Identity Independence

**Identity Independence** keeps conceptual document identity independent of unnecessary repository, storage, programming language or implementation prescriptions. Explicit logical domain, canonicalization, reference, representation and integration constraints remain legitimate owner requirements; actual formats/adapters/executors must preserve them.

Conceptual separation does not guarantee every technology/format can interoperate without adaptation, validation or coordinated change. Preserve compatible meaning where feasible; necessary contract changes require rationale, previous/new owner/consumer mapping, dependencies, compatibility and transition evidence.

**Evidence boundary:** Identify applicable logical requirements and actual adapter/executor observations. This conceptual source supplies no generation/storage algorithm, implemented permission system, universal portability or harmless-extension guarantee.

## 3.11 Identity Reference

An **Identity Reference** uses identity to refer to an intended logical document under qualified domain rules. An exact-edition reference additionally identifies intended coordinates/bytes and relevant context. A reference association is not another identity key; provenance and applicable alias/target interpretation remain explicit.

Relationships owns typed connection records; Document Identity owns document endpoint identity meanings. Other endpoint kinds use their own contracts. Required consumer→provider consumption is separately typed from association, projection, navigation and execution. DID-003/005/014 cardinality/mandatory reference schema differences remain pending.

| Unresolvable | An actual performed check cannot establish the required intended target interpretation/resolution under the applicable reference contract/context | Record target, rules, performed method/observation and coverage; no blanket historical invalidity or perpetual availability inference |

**Coverage and aggregation contract:**

- Declare the identity claim and its applicable mandatory rules before deciding Valid. An arbitrary successful subset is only successful check evidence, not a full Valid identity claim; inapplicability needs responsible justification, not omission to manufacture success.

Do not suppress a specific observation through a silent precedence rule. An overlapping mandatory violation is additionally Invalid only when its applicable rule and violation are established.

Any implementation that also needs one summary field must preserve the full observation set and disclose its explicit summary mapping without changing these meanings or manufacturing completeness.
- Contradictory governing contracts are recorded as authority/applicability limitations; they do not alone prove that the assessed subject violated a rule. Evaluate unambiguous subsets with explicit limits, and obtain responsible owner reconciliation before broader conformance claims.
- A later input/rule/context change requires assessment of the resulting artifacts. Earlier Valid, local PASS or stable logical identity does not automatically validate changed bytes, publish/approve them or select a Baseline.

This result contract is independent of how a checker is implemented. It supplies no operational checker, allocation, resolver, universal future guarantee or whole-framework certification.

---

## 9.5. Governance

Governance is the area grouping Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines, not a new component. Applicable owners can require identity checks and define documentary decision/evidence conditions without redefining identity semantics. Reviews records examined scope/findings; Baselines needs actual exact approved-edition selection, not merely an identity-check result.

Validation, formal approval, publication, exact edition Status and snapshot membership remain distinct events. DMS/tool/manual processes execute actual operations and CMS governs changes in its scope. A local validation outcome grants none of those other decisions automatically.

---

# 10. Architectural Constraints

The six original constraint responsibilities remain with explicit subjects and conditions.

|---|---|

| Never modify identities | Checking does not mutate the assessed key or silently repair input evidence; result/evidence output is a separate record |
| Never generate identities | No allocation, key creation or silent target substitution to satisfy a check; remediation is a separately governed action |
| Deterministic | For equivalent pinned inputs, rules and relevant observation context, apply stable owner meanings; disclose live/nondeterministic dependencies and actual context instead of context-free promises |
| Repeatable | Retain sufficient exact artifact/rule/context/method provenance to reproduce or explain the observations within stated limits; changed inputs/rules/context require new assessment |
| Implementation independent | Owner semantics do not choose a runtime; actual executors still meet applicable representation/interface/evidence obligations |

A result report may be written without modifying the assessed identity. Corrections to a working document or generated records need their own authorized change/version/provenance and later validation; validation itself is not permission for mutation. Record original evidence and actual failures rather than retrospectively converting them into success. No long-term/global outcome guarantee follows from these requirements.

- document publication;
- document lifecycle management;

| Received compliance condition | Qualified requirement and actual evidence boundary |
|---|---|
| Identifier is unique | Full qualified domain/key/canonical interpretation over declared actual population/history, with collision/reservation limits |

A partial successful check is not full identity, peer or framework conformity; no automatic approval, publication or Baseline follows.

Mandatory State/Canonical Reference and complete-record/lifecycle/constraint authority in DID-005/006/014 remain actual owner work. Do not waive requirements, invent a merged record or select a conflicting rule merely to claim success. | Assigning multiple identities to the same document | Competing allocations contrary to the applicable document/domain/canonical contract; exact editions, aliases or representations are not automatically different logical identities |

| Bypassing canonical identity definitions | Actual circumvention of governing responsible rules; common Architecture/Policy and other domain owners remain applicable, and actual peer authority conflicts must be reconciled rather than ignored |

2. Identify responsible semantic owners and actual decision/execution authority for the proposed correction. A review finding, governance label or validation result alone grants no mutation, allocation, operational permission, approval or publication.

Before a necessary normative change or identity/path/representation migration, assess prior/new contract, rationale, affected owners/consumers and actual required dependencies; record compatibility, mappings, reservations/history/aliases/reference and exact-snapshot continuity plus transition checks.

No source ID migration, allocation, actual correction operation or global remediation is executed by this procedure description.

| Technology independent | Identity meaning is not defined by a platform; applicable logical representation/interface/adapter requirements and actual evidence can still matter |

No implementation technology is prescribed here. That does not prohibit legitimate logical format/canonicalization/interface constraints or evidence about actual adapters/executors. Independence does not prove implemented interoperability, fully separate required dependencies or universal future outcomes. Record exact rules/artifacts/context, checks, executor, observations, coverage and limits.

## 4.1. DID-C-001 — Identity Existence

Preserve the assigned qualified key's association with the same logical document under its governing contract through ordinary content, classification, location, representation and edition/status evolution. ## 4.3. DID-C-003 — Identity Immutability

An actual conformance claim shall identify its exact subject/domain, artifacts/editions/bytes and context, applicable responsible mandatory rules/source editions/interfaces, executor/method, performed/unperformed checks, observations, population/coverage and limitations. # 2. Introduction

Although the recommendations presented here are not normative requirements, they can guide the application of independently applicable mandatory owner contracts. The advisory wording does not waive those contracts or introduce new universal mandatory rules. Type Reference identifies the document's consultation responsibility; explicit applicable declarations and references, not Type, title or directory, determine authority.

Read each recommendation against its intended subject, responsible domain rules and exact source editions. Preserve unresolved mandatory State/Canonical Reference/lifecycle, extension and required-interface authority rather than inventing an accepted merged contract or selecting a conflicting rule to claim success.

# 4. Identity Assignment

The three original assignment recommendations remain. Apply them to actual intended normalized document/domain subjects and responsible allocation decisions; these recommendations supply no generation algorithm or universal assignment time.

---

## 4.1. Assign Identity Once

Recommend one governing assignment for the applicable logical document under its domain contract, with actual allocation/association authority and collision/reservation/history evidence. Architectural recognition, a file's creation, registration or a generated header is not by itself assignment.

Ordinary content, metadata, classification, location, format and edition/status evolution should preserve the assigned key. Copies and exact editions of the same document do not automatically need new identities. A genuinely different logical document needs its own applicable subject/allocation assessment; necessary governing-contract transitions follow §5.2 rather than being disguised as ordinary evolution.

---

## 4.2. Assign Identity Early

Recommend establishing an applicable document's identity early enough to support its actual traceability needs, when the responsible domain and allocation decision/evidence are available. Governance entry alone neither allocates a key nor proves authority, uniqueness or which lifecycle assertion applies.

Pre-allocation subjects and excluded functional files remain distinct. Do not invent an identity or reservation simply to satisfy an early-assignment recommendation, and do not infer an organizational role or permission from authorship, file custody or architectural naming.

---

## 4.3. Avoid Temporary Identities

Avoid presenting temporary tracking labels as canonical assigned document identities. Where provisional tracking is necessary, distinguish its subject, scope and responsible record from the governing Domain+Identifier key; no new universal lifecycle state or Metadata Element is defined here.

Canonical assignment still needs the actual responsible domain/series decision and collision/reservation/history evidence. Preserve traceable provisional-to-assigned interpretation, original records and affected reference/context mappings without silently promoting a placeholder, fabricating a past allocation or retargeting historical evidence. A matching string alone is not that decision.

---

# 5. Identity Preservation

The three original preservation subjects remain. Recommend preserving assigned same-document identity while separately assessing actual record, representation, reference, consumer and decision effects.

---

## 5.1. Preserve Identity During Revisions

Content revisions, corrections, restructurings, metadata and classification changes should preserve the assigned qualified key under its governing contract. Supporting state/reference/descriptor/registration/projection records and documentary Version/Revision/Status can change under their own responsible rules.

Keep exact changed artifacts, contributors, applicable source editions and observations traceable. Preserving logical identity does not automatically validate changed bytes, merge conflicting mandatory records or extend an earlier validation result to a successor.

---

## 5.2. Preserve Identity During Migration

Repository, storage and technology movement should preserve the assigned logical key through ordinary migration. Actual locators, indexes, aliases, freshness, interfaces and references can be affected; examine prior/new representations and intended targets rather than assuming the movement is harmless.

Before a necessary normative/domain/path/representation transition, recommend identifying prior/new responsible rules and actual authority, rationale/alternatives, exact affected semantic/record owners, consumers and indispensable interfaces. Assess compatibility and document exact mappings/qualification, canonical aliases, collisions/reservations/history, same-document continuity and reference/exact-edition/pinned-snapshot effects. Preserve allocated/retired non-reuse and never silently reassign a key to another document or retarget an immutable historical member.

Apply only the separately authorized scoped change with actual contribution, edition/history and transition evidence; retain original failed checks and later validate the resulting exact artifacts. Advice or a local PASS alone grants no migration or mutation. No migration is executed by this document.

---

## 5.3. Preserve Identity During Publication

Different published formats or physical copies of the same logical document should preserve its governing identity rather than automatically allocate additional document keys. Exact editions, representations and publication records remain distinguishable with their source/context evidence.

Publication, formal approval and Baseline membership are separate decisions. A Draft successor does not inherit received Canonical naming, approval or selection into Baseline1.0. Preserve immutable historical exact-edition selections and relevant pinned relation context; a current path or stable identity alone does not identify an exact approved member.

---

# 6. Identifier Management

The three original identifier-management subjects remain. Recommend responsible qualified interpretation and stable assigned allocation, not a context-free string convention or running resolver.

---

## 6.1. Prefer Stable Identifiers

Preserve the assigned canonical identifier interpretation and same-document association through ordinary evolution under its governing Domain+Identifier contract. Distinguish that key from a canonical rendering, location, alias, descriptor or exact edition.

For this corpus the domain is Documentation Framework, represented by DF. DF-SSS-NNN uses a registered uppercase three-letter stable allocation series and positive three-digit001–999 allocation. 000 is not allocated; allocated/retired numbers remain reserved, and gaps prove no availability. At999, register a traceable unused continuation series rather than widen syntax or recycle. Current Family/Type/Component/path/status/edition does not reconstruct an assigned key. Other domains need their own explicit contracts.

Actual uniqueness needs responsible canonicalization, assignments, population/collision/reservation/history and coverage evidence. Syntax or a partial index is not proof of global uniqueness or availability. Necessary governing-contract transitions use §5.2; this source allocates or renumbers no key.

---

## 6.2. Avoid Semantic Encoding

Avoid deriving a governing key from values expected to change. The five original examples remain:

- repository names;
- storage locations;
- workflow states;
- file paths;
- implementation technologies.

Current mutable Family/Type/Component and metadata values likewise should not regenerate an assigned key. A registered stable series may retain a recorded historical origin or purpose without encoding the document's current classification. Do not renumber an existing valid identifier merely because that historical series code is meaningful. Domain prefixes and legitimate canonical representations remain governed by their responsible contracts, not rejected merely as semantic encoding.

## 6.3. Maintain Identifier Consistency

Recommend consistent intended qualified document identity and canonical interpretation across document-targeting references. Exact-edition references additionally need the responsible coordinates/bytes and context. Other endpoint kinds follow their own typed identity contracts; not every architectural reference targets a document.

Legitimate aliases, alternative representations and adapters need logical/domain mappings, responsible source/edition provenance and actual interface compatibility; they are not solely implementation design choices. Repeated renderings of one intended key are not alone competing allocations.

Incoming references may be0..N; optional incoming population does not waive validity of each actual reference. # 7. Cross-Component Integration

Distinguish identity semantic ownership under common Architecture/Policy from actual descriptor/category/connection/registration/projection owners and other entity domains. Documentary authority, required consumption, projection, navigation and execution have different meanings.

## 7.1. Metadata

Metadata should associate descriptors with the intended applicable document or exact edition/context without redefining document-key meaning. Its Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance and other subject/entity contracts remain separate. Traceable representation of identity values, with responsible source/edition provenance, is not itself prohibited duplication or a competing allocation.

Metadata→Document Identity is the actual required identification claim for the applicable normalized document described. The functional DID README also states: “The Document Identity component depends on the Metadata component for the canonical definition of metadata concepts used to describe document identity.” Current DID-009§5.1.1/§10 retains both claims. Recommend keeping these actual reciprocal requirements explicit pending responsible core-versus-descriptor/interface/source-edition reconciliation; projection or navigation relabelling does not dissolve a genuine required cycle.

No absent Metadata Element/Profile, mandatory state or approval fact is invented by representing identity information.

---

## 7.2. Classification

Classification should categorize the intended document under its own category/assignment contracts and consume the applicable document-key meaning without redefining it. Category/definition/entity keys are not automatically normalized document IDs. Changes to current classification labels do not reconstruct an assigned stable document series/key.

---

## 7.3. Registry

Registry entries should identify their intended qualified document or exact edition/context with source provenance and freshness limits. Registration/index records retain Registry ownership; internal entry keys and locators do not replace canonical document identity.

Repeated entries or copied key values are not alone duplicate allocations. Registration is distinct from allocation, approval and completeness of population/history checks. No mandatory universal Registry intermediary or running lookup service is implied.

---

## 7.4. Relationships

Relationships should preserve typed connection/endpoints and provenance under its owner contracts. Document endpoints use the intended qualified document/exact-edition context in §6.3; other endpoint types keep their own identity rules.

An actual connection still needs its applicable type/direction/subject/context and observed validity; canonical target identity alone does not establish the whole connection's correctness or permanent retrieval. Connection changes do not allocate identity, authorize silent target replacement or redefine the document key.

## 7.5. Knowledge Graph

Document nodes should preserve intended qualified document-key meaning while Knowledge Graph owns logical node/edge projection and mutable properties. Source identity and Relationships connection records remain authoritative with actual edition/context provenance and refresh limits.

Knowledge Graph→Document Identity for document nodes and Knowledge Graph→Relationships for typed connections are selected required contracts, not removed because data is projected. Logical representation/interface requirements are architectural responsibilities; storage/runtime choices remain implementation concerns. Derived records do not establish competing authority, new allocation, synchronized consumers or complete graph/acyclicity proof.

# 8. Governance Recommendations

Governance is the area grouping Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines, not one operational engine. Applicable DMS, tool or manual processes execute actual operations, with CMS governing changes in its scope.

Logical identity, publication copies and validation results alone select no member. Draft successors do not inherit approval/membership or retarget immutable history. # 11. Common Anti-Patterns

Avoid reassigning allocated or retired keys to a different logical document. Preserve original association, actual retirement scope/decision, reservations and history. Missing index records or unavailable content is neither availability nor proof an observed reassignment occurred. Gaps do not authorize reuse, and advice does not execute retirement or allocation.

Avoid arbitrary or nonconforming changes to the assigned qualified key/same-document association. Necessary governing-contract/domain/representation transitions first need §5.2 responsible prior/new authority, owner/consumer, compatibility/history/reference/snapshot assessment; no blanket arbitrary mutation is recommended.

---

## 11.4. Repository-Dependent Identities

Avoid reconstructing a document key from mutable repository paths, folders or custody. Repository locators, internal entry keys and source-control representations can legitimately change or map to an existing key under their contracts. Preserve assigned identity and actual prior/new references/index freshness/history; such adapters are not automatically repository-dependent competing semantics.

---

## 11.5. Technology-Dependent Identities

Avoid letting implementation choices silently redefine governing document-key/domain meaning or derive unstable keys from mutable technologies. Legitimate domain-preserving serialization, language structures, storage/API mappings and explicitly governed representation/interface constraints are distinct from semantic redefinition. A registered domain prefix or stable historical series code is not automatically a violation merely because its representation has technical form.

## 11.6. Workflow-Dependent Identities

State/edition/result record changes do not alone alter identity; deletion or archiving alone is not logical retirement or approval of a missing transition.

## 11.7. Metadata-Derived Identities

                Unassigned

                    ▼

                Preserved

                    ▼

                 Retired

The lifecycle describes the existence of the identity itself rather than the operational state of the document.

# 5. Conceptual Principles

## 5.1. AP-001 — Documentation as Knowledge

Documentation shall represent organized knowledge through logical entities, identified sources and applicable contracts. A file is a representation, not automatically a registered capability or a complete knowledge system. Normalized sources and functional files contribute within their respective scopes; DF defines documentary requirements while an applicable process produces/manages representations.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess purpose, actual source organization, relationships and coverage. The principle creates neither a document component nor proof that every file contributes complete or consistent knowledge.

---

## 5.2. AP-002 — Explicit Architecture

Architectural decisions shall identify the subject, scope, responsible owners, assumptions, applicable contracts and rationale explicitly. Significant allocation, classification, identity or required-contract changes require previous/new mapping and affected editions before propagation. Record unresolved decisions or missing evidence rather than treating an implicit label, arrow or directory as authority.

**Evidence boundary:** Examine actual decision/owner/reference records and limits. Explicit documentation proves neither approval nor complete implementation; derived summaries preserve authoritative provenance.

---

## 5.3. AP-003 — Technology Independence

Architectural definitions shall avoid prescribing technology unless an explicit integration constraint requires it. Logical identity, classification and domain meaning are distinct from filenames, formats, repositories and storage technology. Actual implementations still require representations, adapters, interfaces and executors under their applicable contracts.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess declared technology constraints and actual representation/adapter compatibility. Conceptual independence does not guarantee every format/tool is suitable, an implementation exists or technologies can evolve without consumer impact.

---

## 5.4. AP-004 — Single Source of Truth

Each semantic concept or authoritative record shall have one identified responsible owner within its declared domain/scope. Metadata Dictionary defines descriptor meaning while Identity, Classification and Governance retain their domain semantics. Traceable summaries, catalogs and projections may repeat derived values with source-edition provenance and refresh/state limits without acquiring competing authority.

**Evidence boundary:** Check responsible definition/record sources, derived-copy provenance and unresolved conflicts. Logical single authority does not require one physical copy, a universal Registry route or a complete canonical catalog merely from this principle.

---

## 5.5. AP-005 — Semantic Consistency

Consuming representations shall preserve applicable owner meanings and identify subjects/qualified contexts. Controlled aliases and historic vocabulary retain explicit mappings; unqualified overloads or competing meanings are recorded and reconciled. Metadata represents domain values, Schema organizes references, Profile constrains usage and Instance provides values under one effective Profile without redefining semantics.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess actual definitions, profiles, represented values and consumer scope. This principle does not manufacture missing Element/Profile records or prove consistency of unseen sources.

---

# 6. Structural Principles

## 6.1. AP-006 — Separation of Responsibilities

Each registered capability shall have a defined primary semantic responsibility and primary allocation. Explicit collaboration, cross-cutting participation, shared check domains and traceable projections are permitted while preserving owner boundaries. Reviews may use Validation/Consistency Verification results without acquiring their rule ownership or approval authority.

**Evidence boundary:** Check primary owner/consumer contracts and actual support interactions. Prevent competing semantics rather than prohibiting every overlap of supporting work; no new capability or reassignment is inferred from a concern or directory.

---

## 6.2. AP-007 — Layered Architecture

Structural allocation shall follow Architectural Layers:seven areas are Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation and Integration. Foundation/Architecture supply supporting definitions; the supplied 23 capabilities retain their 4/4/5/5/5 allocation. Five conceptual concerns—Knowledge, Documentation, Governance, Discovery and Preservation—are a different view.

**Evidence boundary:** For required cross-Layer consumption, record consumer→provider contract/scope/source editions and apply the declared support order:the provider precedes its consumer. Same-Layer requirements, including Knowledge Graph→Relationships and Workflow→Policies, need explicit interfaces/ownership and cycle assessment. There is no obligation to consume every earlier provider or an adjacent serial service chain. Genuine required cycles are prohibited in the governed scope and remain visible for reconciliation; no projection/reference label hides them. Changing constraints requires assessed architectural revision, not an arbitrary upward exception. These rules certify neither a full graph nor implemented layer services.

---

## 6.3. AP-008 — Modular Design

Components shall preserve coherent boundaries and compatible provider contracts where feasible. Separate areas or documents may still require coordinated content/descriptor, owner/consumer or release changes. Independent evolution is an assessed objective under actual dependencies, not an unconditional guarantee.

**Evidence boundary:** Map affected exact editions, provider compatibility and transition evidence. A new component or module label alone proves neither independent release nor operational modularity.

---

## 6.4. AP-009 — Explicit Relationships

Applicable connections shall be explicitly typed with identified endpoints and provenance. Distinguish documentary authority references, semantic associations, representation/projection, navigation, required consumption and execution. A required edge names consumer, provider, contract, scope and responsible source editions; physical directories, names and visual order alone establish no edge.

**Evidence boundary:** Check actual connection records and resolvable endpoints. Preserve genuine requirements/cycles visibly and reconcile conflicting owner contracts; do not rename an indispensable provider as navigation to create apparent acyclicity. This principle imposes no nonempty relationship list on every file.

---

## 6.5. AP-010 — Stable Identity

Normalized documents shall preserve valid permanent logical identity under the applicable Domain+Identifier allocation/preservation contract. Identifier representation, current classification, title, Version/Revision, Status and physical location are distinct facts. Existing valid DF-SSS-NNN allocations do not automatically change with Family/Type or path; necessary migration needs a mapped assessed identity change.

**Evidence boundary:** Apply the functional-file exclusion in §3 first:README.md, CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md require no normalized ID by this principle. Assess actual uniqueness/resolution and collision evidence; no 000 functional identity, missing allocation or universal generation algorithm is invented.

---

# 8. Evolution Principles

## 8.1. AP-015 — Incremental Evolution

Prefer incremental architectural improvement where it can meet actual requirements while preserving compatible meaning. A necessary larger or foundational change can be justified when incremental alternatives cannot adequately satisfy identified responsibilities or constraints.

**Evidence boundary:** Record previous/new contracts, alternatives/rationale, affected owners/consumers, dependencies and transition/verification evidence. Avoid disruption where feasible without an absolute ban on justified incompatible reconciliation.

---

## 8.2. AP-016 — Backward Compatibility

Preserve compatible meaning and provider/consumer contracts where feasible. Necessary incompatible changes shall be explicitly justified with affected exact editions, previous/new mappings, reference/identity effects, transition evidence and verification limits. Compatibility is assessed from contracts, not from names, folder layout or a Version label alone.

**Evidence boundary:** For this working document review, compatible correction retains Version; compatible additive capability increments minor; incompatible contract change increments major and resets minor to 0. Every changed persisted edition increments Revision monotonically across Version changes. Validation of unchanged source changes neither coordinate and is tracked centrally. Domain-specific entity numbering requires its own qualified owner; no completed consumer rollout is inferred.

---

## 8.3. AP-017 — Extensibility

Introduce a new capability or source role only for a demonstrated need with defined owner responsibility, primary allocation, typed interactions and consumer impact. Reuse or extend existing contracts where feasible. Necessary changes to foundations, responsibilities or interfaces are permitted through the assessed evolution process in AP-015/016 and §14; extension-only is not an absolute prohibition on foundational revision.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess whether existing meaning/functionality changes, actual dependencies and transition evidence. A new capability is not assumed harmless and need not create another Layer. No component, Metadata Element, Profile or specification is fabricated merely to make an extension appear complete.

---

## 8.4. AP-018 — Architectural Stability

Preserve coherent conceptual boundaries and compatible owner meanings where feasible. Implementation technologies can evolve under applicable representation/provider/consumer contracts; their independence is not guaranteed by conceptual separation. Necessary semantic changes retain source history and explicit compatibility/version transition.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess actual contracts, affected editions and integration/adapter constraints. Stability is a controlled design objective, not foundation immutability, harmless extension or a guarantee of unchanged semantics for every future edition.

Where an actual required cycle or conflicting provider declaration is found, retain it visibly in the evidence and reconcile the responsible contracts/allocations. This working source does not certify a complete cycle-free framework graph.
